## Summary
17 verified Capterra reviews (rating 4.6/5, 4.1 ease-of-use, 4.8 customer service) from real Infigo admins/developers. The most useful third-party signal on what working with Infigo actually feels like — including direct comparisons to ROI360, XMPie Circle, Pressero, PressWise, MyOrderDesk, and PersonalEffect StoreFlow from people who switched.

## Key takeaways

**Why admins picked Infigo over competitors (their words):**
- Sean O. (Talient Action Group), switched from XMPie Circle: "Most of the other systems we reviewed did not have any where near the editor tools that Catfish offered. They were more MIS systems mixed with Web2Print features. Catfish focuses on the storefront and does very well with it." XMPie's "required customization … was driving extremely slow implementation and release."
- Jesse B. (Peczuh Printing), switched from Pressero: "The existing depth of integration with our MIS, Tharstern and the room for growth far outmatched Pressero's."
- Chris H. (Education): rejected Pressero — "None of the other softwares provides the level of dynamic templates we were looking for."
- Tony W. switched from MyOrderDesk; chose Infigo over PersonalEffect StoreFlow because XMPie design team was slow/limited.
- Dan P. (10-year user): switched from ROI360 and earlier Infigo versions where "even small changes felt difficult"; the template tools made content updates "incredibly easy … without relying on code."

**Recurring pros (themes across multiple reviewers):**
- Storefront-first DNA (vs. competitors that are MIS bolted to W2P).
- Two template engines (Infigo Designer + MegaEdit) — "endless product applications."
- "Cookie cut" themes/sites enable fast multi-portal rollout.
- AWS hosting, fast/reliable, frequent releases (weekly).
- Support team is repeatedly singled out as the differentiator — 12-hour turnaround typical.
- The entire website (not just the storefront) can run on Infigo — used as full CMS by Dan P.

**Recurring cons (operator pain points — read this carefully):**
- **JavaScript required for advanced templates.** Multiple reviewers: "Advanced templates do require quite a bit of JavaScript knowledge and programming." Chris H.: "if you have someone in-house that knows JavaScript then it's a piece of cake" — implicit warning if you don't.
- **Documentation gaps on advanced scripting / APIs / newer features.** Sean F. (Bitstorm/Think Patented): "many areas in the backend that aren't documented or have cryptic descriptions, so you're not sure what they do unless you try it and see, or reach out to support."
- **Rapid evolution = navigation drift.** Dan P.: "features moving or changing as updates roll out."
- **Settings sprawl.** Jason L.: "Multiple settings are not available to admins and must be managed by support."
- **Two editors to learn.** Jesse B.: "having two to choose from and two to learn makes it difficult to master both."
- **Specific functional gaps (Jesse B./Peczuh, 2021):** No high-res proofing online, no file catalog for customers, no front-end order overview save approval, no inventory dashboard.
- **Bidirectional MIS data flow limits (Jesse B./Peczuh, 2021):** "Not being able to pass order related data back to Catfish from Tharstern has made some parts more manual."
- **Acrobat plugin is 32-bit (Sean F., 2020):** Infigo Designer template creator plugin not supported on latest macOS/Acrobat — blocks macOS upgrades. (Infigo's reply: replaced by InDesign plugin.)
- **Limited shipping integration:** Tony W. flagged FedEx integration as a disappointment.
- **MFA email setup:** Jeremiah M. (Peczuh) flagged email setup with MFA as not easy.
